guide.a.what_are_email_notifications: When configured, the system can send up to two emails after each successful registration: a confirmation email to the attendee (if they provided an email address) with their ticket details and link, and a notification email to the business email address (if one is set) letting you know someone has booked. Emails are sent in the background and won't delay the booking process.
guide.a.supported_email_providers:
Five providers are supported, all using HTTP APIs (no SMTP required):

  • Resend
  • Postmark
  • SendGrid
  • Mailgun (US)
  • Mailgun (EU)

All providers work the same way — choose whichever you already have an account with or whichever offers a free tier that suits your volume.
guide.q.setup_email: How do I set up email?
guide.a.setup_email:
Email is already configured by your server administrator using {hostEmailProvider} with from address {hostEmailFromAddress}. You can override this by entering your own provider and API key in Settings. If you provide your own settings, they take priority over the server configuration.

  1. Go to Settings and find the Email section
  2. Choose your email provider from the dropdown
  3. Paste your provider's API key into the API Key field
  4. Enter a From Address — this is the sender address that appears on outgoing emails. If left blank, the business email address is used instead
  5. Save the settings

The from address must be a verified sender in your email provider's account, otherwise emails will be rejected. Check your provider's documentation for how to verify a sender domain or address.
guide.q.test_email_working: How do I test that email is working?
guide.a.test_email_working: After saving your email settings, a Send Test Email button appears. Click it to send a test email to your business email address. If the test fails, you'll see the HTTP status code and the error message from your provider. That message usually names the fix — most often a wrong API key, or a from address the provider has not verified.
guide.q.email_not_configured: What if email is not configured?
guide.a.email_not_configured: Email is entirely optional. If no provider is selected, the system skips sending emails silently. Registrations, payments, webhooks, and everything else continue to work normally.
guide.q.confirmation_email_content: What does the confirmation email contain?
guide.a.confirmation_email_content: The attendee receives an email with the listing name(s), quantity, price paid, and a clickable link to their ticket page. Each email also includes an SVG ticket image as an attachment — one per listing, with a QR code for check-in. For No check-in listings the QR code is omitted because buyers do not need to be checked in. For multi-listing bookings, all listings are listed in a single email with numbered ticket attachments. The business email is set as the reply-to address so attendees can reply directly to you.
guide.q.admin_notification_email_content: What does the admin notification email contain?
guide.a.admin_notification_email_content: You receive an email showing the attendee's name, email, phone, address, and any special instructions, along with the listing name(s), quantity, and price. The attendee's email is set as the reply-to address so you can reply directly to them.
guide.q.customise_emails: Can I customise the emails that are sent?
guide.a.customise_emails:
Yes. In Settings, scroll to the email template sections. You can customise both the confirmation email (sent to the attendee) and the admin notification email (sent to you). Each has three parts: subject line, HTML body, and plain text body.

Templates use Liquid syntax. Clear any field to revert to the built-in default.
guide.q.template_variables: What variables can I use in templates?
guide.q.template_error: What happens if my template has an error?
guide.a.template_error: If a custom template fails to render, the system falls back to the built-in default template automatically. The email is still sent — your attendees won't miss their confirmation.
guide.q.how_do_i_email_a_group_of: How do I email a group of attendees?
guide.a.how_do_i_email_a_group_of: Open Emails in the top navigation (owners only), or click Email Attendees on a listing page to message that listing's attendees. Choose who receives it, write your message in Markdown, tick marketing if it's promotional, then click Preview. The preview shows the rendered email, the exact recipient count, and what kind of message it is before you send.
guide.a.who_can_i_send_to:
From a listing page, the recipients are that listing's attendees. From the Emails page you pick an audience:

  • Active listing attendees — everyone booked onto a currently-active listing (the default).
  • Upcoming listing attendees — everyone booked onto an active listing that hasn't happened yet.
  • All attendees — everyone who has ever registered.

In every case, only attendees who gave an email address are included, and duplicate addresses are removed automatically.
guide.a.how_does_unsubscribing_work:
Every marketing email includes an unsubscribe link. It opens a page where the recipient can unsubscribe (or resubscribe) with a single click — no login needed. The link identifies them by a one-way hash of their address, so the page never reveals or exposes the email address itself, and the action only happens on a button press, never just by opening the link.

Unsubscribes apply to marketing emails only. Transactional/service messages about a booking still reach everyone.
guide.q.what_is_the_bcc_email_app_option: What is the BCC email-app option?
guide.a.what_is_the_bcc_email_app_option: On the preview page there's always an option to open the email in your own mail app with the subject and body pre-filled. When it's going to several people they all go in BCC (with the draft addressed from your business email) so they can't see each other; a single recipient is simply addressed directly. It needs no provider setup, so it works even when system sending is disabled. Use it sparingly though — sending lots of mail this way, especially marketing, is a quick way to get your personal email account rate-limited or blocked. It's best for small, genuinely transactional messages.
guide.q.why_do_i_need_my_own_email: Why do I need my own email provider to send?
guide.a.why_do_i_need_my_own_email:
Bulk email sends through your own configured email provider, not any shared/host email. Sending marketing from a shared address would put every site on the platform at risk of being flagged as spam. If you haven't added your own provider (under Advanced Settings → Email Notifications), the Send button is disabled — but you can still use the BCC email-app option (see below).

Bulk email goes out through your provider's batch API, so all supported providers (Resend, Postmark, SendGrid, and Mailgun) can send it.
guide.q.what_s_the_difference_between_a_: What's the difference between a marketing and a transactional email?
guide.a.what_s_the_difference_between_a_:
A transactional (service) email is essential information about a listing someone booked — a venue change, a reminder, cancellation details. A marketing email promotes something — a new listing, an offer, a newsletter.

When you tick marketing, every email gets an unsubscribe footer, and anyone who has previously unsubscribed is skipped automatically. Transactional emails get no footer and reach everyone. Only mark genuine promotions as marketing — mislabelling promotions as transactional to dodge the unsubscribe rules can breach anti-spam laws (such as GDPR/PECR or CAN-SPAM).
guide.q.can_i_see_how_often_i_ve: Can I see how often I've contacted someone?
guide.a.can_i_see_how_often_i_ve:
Yes. Each attendee's page shows an Email History — how many bulk emails they've received, when they were last contacted, and the last subject — so you can avoid over-emailing. When you preview a bulk email, a line summarises how often that audience has been contacted on average, so you get a sense of the group before you send.

Counts cover bulk emails only (not per-booking confirmations) and are tracked against a one-way hash of the address, so the history follows the person even across separate bookings.
